issue.title: Both test_ace_and_lsp_include_dispatch_* parity nodes fail under the full parallel lane, pass in isolation
issue.description:
FOUND BY the sase-xz.land agent while consuming `just check-full` monitor 4fvbspmpxjw5
(landing gate for epic sase-xz, file-aware pager syntax highlighting). Every lint gate,
SASE validation, committed plans, and the whole `just test-cost` full suite passed; the
only failing step was the last one, `just selection-health --fail-on-new-flake`, which
promoted these two nodes with no entry in tests/reproducible_flake_baseline.txt.

Two nodes, one root cause, one bead: they co-fail in all three promoting records and
never appear apart.

- tests/test_xprompt_directive_completion_parity.py::test_ace_and_lsp_include_dispatch_directive_when_enabled
- tests/test_xprompt_directive_completion_parity.py::test_ace_and_lsp_include_dispatch_machine_rows_when_enabled

NOT caused by epic sase-xz. Neither promoting head is a sase-xz commit (50b1405f4
"feat(dispatch): launch agents on remote machines" x2 and a0fcc5ade "feat(pager): thread
link context through entry points", which belongs to epic sase-xy), and the ACE/LSP
directive-completion parity path has nothing to do with pager syntax highlighting.

`just selection-health --fail-on-new-flake` is the last gate of `just check-full`, so an
undeclared node here blocks every landing agent that reaches it. This bead is filed so
the nodes can carry a baseline entry with a named owner.

Both tests start a real `sase-xprompt-lsp` subprocess through LspSession and assert that
the `%dispatch` directive rows the LSP offers match ACE's own completion rows while the
remote_dispatch flag is enabled. Leading hypothesis, not proven: the installed
`sase_core_rs` extension or the installed `sase-xprompt-lsp` binary is older than the
sase-core checkout and therefore does not know the `%dispatch` vocabulary that landed
with 50b1405f4. Both records at that head co-fail
`tests/test_check_sase_core_rs_bindings_tool.py::test_dev_extension_exposes_every_collected_name`
and `tests/test_xprompt_directive_contract.py::test_runtime_directive_vocabulary_matches_core_contract`,
which is the exact signature of a stale extension; ready bug sase-v6 documents
`rust-lsp-install` copying from the wrong cargo target dir and exiting 0 after the copy
fails. The a0fcc5ade record, however, was a clean tree with no such co-failure, so
staleness alone may not explain every occurrence.

payload.entry:
SUPPLEMENTARY EVIDENCE (same reporter family, sase-xz.land--3; recorded as a note rather than a +1). The third `just check-full` landing attempt for epic sase-xz (monitor nppac98sb90a) promoted two MORE nodes over the reproducible-flake baseline, both belonging to this bead's root cause:

- tests/test_xprompt_directive_completion_parity.py::test_ace_and_lsp_directive_argument_rows_match[%dispatch:]
- tests/test_xprompt_directive_contract.py::test_runtime_directive_vocabulary_matches_core_contract

Both pass in isolation in this workspace (2 passed in 2.54s at head e5106d490).

ROOT CAUSE IS SHARPER THAN THE ORIGINAL HYPOTHESIS, AND IT IS NOT AN LSP PROBLEM. tests/test_xprompt_directive_contract.py::test_runtime_directive_vocabulary_matches_core_contract imports sase_core_rs directly and asserts `set(contract) == set(_KNOWN_DIRECTIVES) | {alt, xprompts_enabled}` plus a literal keyword table containing \"dispatch\". It has no LspSession, no subprocess and no async pilot, yet it co-fails with the %dispatch parity nodes in EVERY promoting record. That rules out the LspSession/xprompt-lsp-install limb of this bead's hypothesis and isolates the single shared ingredient: a compiled sase_core_rs in the running workspace whose directive contract predates the %dispatch vocabulary added by sase-xe's 50b1405f4. This is a stale-extension-build failure that looks like a flake because it is workspace-local, not a timing race - which also explains why every node passes in isolation on a workspace whose extension was rebuilt.

NEW PROMOTING RECORDS, ALL FROM OTHER WORKSPACES (none from the sase-xz landing workspace):
- 20260907T214036Z-837b1634ae9e-3936261-full-run.json (workspace sase_34, 5 failures, all in this family)
- 20260907T221947Z-e0c5755033ff-454889-full-run.json (workspace sase_12, 5 failures)
- 20260907T223453Z-d8a299c2c3e4-719425-full-run.json (workspace sase_29, 5 failures)
- 20260907T224235Z-837b1634ae9e-901692-full-run.json (workspace sase_30, 6 failures)
plus the two pre-existing sase_27 records at head 50b1405f4 and one 2026-08-23 record (50534e4f8132, sase) for the contract node alone.

STILL NOT CAUSED BY EPIC sase-xz. This workspace's own two full-run records at the epic head e5106d490f89 (20260907T210528Z on a clean tree, and 20260907T223325Z) both recorded exit 0 with zero failures.

The two node IDs above were appended to this bead's stanza in tests/reproducible_flake_baseline.txt so the landing gate stops promoting them without an owner.

payload.entry:
Root-cause evidence from the 06m family (check-full monitor wtg57wkt2vza, landing gate for unrelated phase sase-y3.3): on current master (a948dc25b) these nodes are NOT flaky -- they fail deterministically in isolation, so a reproducible_flake_baseline.txt entry would be the wrong remedy.

Two things changed under this bead since it was filed. (1) The node names here (test_ace_and_lsp_include_dispatch_directive_when_enabled / ..._machine_rows_when_enabled) no longer exist; ac1ba1be9 renamed them to test_ace_and_lsp_include_dispatch_directive / ..._machine_rows. (2) They now fail alongside three more nodes in the same area: test_ace_and_lsp_directive_name_rows_match, test_ace_and_lsp_directive_argument_rows_match[%dispatch:], and tests/test_xprompt_directive_contract.py::test_runtime_directive_vocabulary_matches_core_contract. All 5 fail in a single-file/isolated run.

The cause is cross-repo skew, not test isolation: sase-xe.15 (ac1ba1be9) removed the remote_dispatch flag on the Python side, but sase-core HEAD 9dc37f4 / v0.32.40 still has `"dispatch" => Some("remote_dispatch")` at crates/sase_core/src/editor/wire.rs:598. The Rust LSP therefore still gates dispatch completion rows behind a flag that is off, while the Python ACE side no longer gates -- hence the parity divergence (LSP [] vs ACE rows). This is consistent with the sase-v6 rust-lsp-staleness hypothesis already linked here, but the staleness is in the core source itself, not in the install step.

Full evidence and the proposed fix are recorded as a DISCOVERED ISSUE note on the still-in-progress epic sase-xe, which owns the flag removal.

evidence.note: 06k CI repair independently reproduced all five current dispatch failures with published core 0.32.40 in monitor s251vy4c5k3q. Prepared the actual Rust source fix: remove the retired dispatch feature flag in editor/wire.rs and stale LSP env/initialize/config plumbing; regression tests cover ungated exported contract, name completion, and machine completion. Full core scripts/check.sh passed in e7hshqrcemrz (119 binding tests plus 120 LSP and 7 JSONRPC tests), rebuilt extension/LSP pass all 26 Python directive parity tests, and z72z0msfpw7m passed 39,396 tests. Core fix is still uncommitted/unpublished; seeking required user exception for core publication before finalizing Python pins. Independently ran selection-health after the full suite: its remaining five promoted current node IDs are these same deterministic dispatch failures, so do not add flake allowances. Retire historical evidence only after the corrected core is actually published/pinned and verified.

sase-xe landing-gate monitor 3ssyvcwnpxwd (just check-full in sase_30, 2026-09-08T00:34Z): selection-health --fail-on-new-flake promoted all five skew nodes (the four dispatch parity nodes plus test_runtime_directive_vocabulary_matches_core_contract) while every other gate and the 39,399-test cost lane passed. Confirms the deterministic pinned-core skew analysis from sase-xe note #9, not a parallel-lane flake: all five pass focused on the landing tree after the core-side gate removal and rebuilt binding/LSP. The landing adds a fixed-at 2026-09-08T00:40:36Z retirement block to tests/reproducible_flake_baseline.txt naming sase-xe/sase-y9; expect transient gate re-reds from stale pinned-core trees until sase-core publishes the fix and the pin ratchets.
